note: Rewritten from the species description of Sands (1972); the original is in English, the genus lacks a soldier caste, and only alates and workers are described; measurement tables, figure numbers, type specimens and distribution records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: First in alphabetical order within Group III, but morphologically rather distinctive: the fontanelle of the alate shows marked sexual dimorphism, very conspicuous and especially so in the female, which distinguishes it from the remaining species of the group. The first marginal tooth of the worker mandible is much reduced, a feature of the group; the enteric valve seating lies ventrally in the unopened abdomen, and together with the secondary characters given in the key this distinguishes it from A. brevior, A. obstructus and A. quietus. The worker abdomen is not incised.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule straw yellow; pilosity yellow, rather sparse. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.27, Pcl/Ri 1.85. Apical tooth of the mandibles short, La/Li 0.51, Ra/Ri 0.61; the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is, in surface view, just separate from the molar prominence, composite ratio 10.32; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies distinctly behind the line from the apical to the second marginal tooth, its anterior margin about half the length of the anterior margin of the second marginal tooth, composite ratio 12.71. Fore tibia weakly inflated, Ti/Ty 4.02; third apical spur distinct, slightly shorter than the other two. Mesenteron-proctodeum junction nearly oblique, passing through the middle of the Malpighian nodule; enteric valve seating ventral in the unopened abdomen, weakly trilobate, the third lobe smaller than the two outer lobes, sessile or with a very short neck and attached to the second proctodeal pouch; the membranous wall of the valve bears sparse microspines outside the inner cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule deep sepia brown, very dark above the fontanelle. Fontanelle markedly sexually dimorphic: in the female a large depressed pale brown area, about the size of the compound eye, its surface slightly irregular; in the male a small jet-black elongate ellipse, slightly raised or absent; in both sexes surrounded by a very dark sepia brown flat area larger than the ocellus. Central spot round, flat, minute, sepia brown; postclypeus pale brown to brown, labrum yellow; frontal spot a very inconspicuous brown crescent, its inner ends slightly concave; antennae brown. Pronotum sepia brown, meso- and metanotum brown, the transverse sutures very weak; femora pale yellowish brown, tibiae yellow, tarsi pale yellow. Abdominal tergites and dorsal spiracles sepia brown, ventral spiracles and sternites brown, the middle of the sternites paler; cerci pale yellow. Posterior margin of the head capsule slightly undulate, not evenly rounded; ocellus rather large, separated from the compound eye by less than half its own minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.21–0.22, Pcl/Ra 2.23–2.51, posterior margin arched, median suture absent. Apical tooth of the mandibles short, La/Li 0.52–0.64, Ra/Rj 0.64–0.76; subsidiary tooth of the left mandible clearly separate from the molar prominence in surface view, composite ratio 6.79–8.09; first marginal tooth of the right mandible slightly behind the line from the apical to the second marginal tooth, its anterior margin slightly longer than that of the second marginal tooth. Head pilosity yellowish brown, uneven, not felt-like. Constriction of the meso- and metanotum narrow, M/W 0.23–0.25. Third apical spur of the fore tibia shorter but distinct.
